clue.text: It might indicate "rat" in a French cryptic crossword, in a decorative style

definitions.text: It might indicate "rat" in a French cryptic crossword
definitions.meaning: in French, 'nouveau' means new, and 'new' is a standard anagram signal, so a French setter could put the word for 'art' beside it to mean rearrange ART
the ornate style of design popular around 1900

explanation.surface: A crossword setter imagines how a French colleague would clue a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'art' with the French word for new and you have both a French-style anagram of RAT and the name of the flowing turn-of-the-century style: ART NOUVEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a specific movement rather than a synonym: the ornate, sinuous style of design and architecture popular around 1900.

clue.text: Very old French impressionist briefly turned up

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter
in a down entry, turning something up makes it read bottom to top

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French impressionist painter, without his final S

explanation.surface: An elderly French painter is carried upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Degas is the impressionist famous for his ballet dancers; the clue's 'Very old' also suits him, as he lived into his eighties.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone aged has lived a long time, so is very old.

clue.text: Cunningly resist rat, one guilty of 12 Across

indicators.note: done cunningly, the letters are craftily rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone slyly holds out against an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 Across is TREASON, so the definition asks for a person who commits it; nine letters means the female form. 'Rat' in the surface is itself slang for a betrayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by cross-reference: treason is the crime, and a woman who commits it is a traitress.

clue.text: Fat to be set, trimming both sides

indicators.note: Trimming cuts away the edges, so the phrase loses its first and last letters and the run inside is left.

parts.note: the letters run on unbroken across the words

explanation.surface: Cooking fat is left to solidify and then its edges are trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like the kitchen noun, setting in a dish; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the adjective: an obese person is very fat.

clue.text: Meat cooked in ovens

indicators.note: cooking turns the ingredients into something new

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Meat is roasted in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is so plain it reads as a cookery note; 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: venison is deer meat, one kind of meat.

clue.text: As formerly used in pesticides?

parts.note: the surface reads the ordinary word 'as'; capitalised, it is a chemical symbol
that element was a standard ingredient of insecticides and weedkillers until safer chemicals replaced it

explanation.surface: A remark about how something was once done in pest control.
explanation.walkthrough: As is the chemical symbol for ARSENIC, and the question mark flags that the little word is doing more than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by history: arsenic compounds were widely sprayed as pesticides in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

clue.text: Shed tears when onion, say, is around

indicators.note: a word turned around runs backwards

parts.note: an onion is an example of a bulb, hence 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone cries whenever onions are being chopped nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the real reason onions make you weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British: to blub is to cry, i.e. shed tears.

clue.text: Some baffling official jargon

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

parts.note: baffLING Official

explanation.surface: Officials speak in bewildering bureaucratic language.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, and the surface is a fair description of the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: lingo is the specialised vocabulary of a trade or group, which is what jargon is.

clue.text: Vessel capsized by figure working around island terminus

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is upside down, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: SUB, a submarine, turned upside down
a stat is a statistic, a figure
I = island
on = working, as a machine is

explanation.surface: A boat overturns because someone is busy near an island's far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminus' reads as the far end of the island in the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a terminus is where routes end, and a bus station is where bus routes start and finish.

clue.text: Uplift characters in chapel at evensong

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: chapEL AT Evensong

explanation.surface: Worshippers are lifted in spirit at the evening service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in the congregation; it means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to elate someone is to lift their spirits.

clue.text: Sling nets around chicks

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone throws nets over young birds to catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it describes the nets encircling the birds; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nestlings are young birds not yet able to leave the nest, i.e. chicks.

clue.text: Less weighty method of kindling fire

definitions.meaning: the comparative of an adjective meaning not heavy
a small device that makes a flame, as for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A suggestion for starting a fire that needs less heavy gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one phrase; split them after 'weighty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the comparative of light (not heavy); the noun is the pocket flame-maker, loosely a 'method' of kindling.

clue.text: Treachery, ultimately without inducement

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of withouT
a reason is an inducement or motive to act

explanation.surface: Someone betrays others in the end with no motive at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking; it only supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of treachery.

clue.text: Grand hammer and mortar

parts.note: G = grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to hammer an opponent is to rout them

explanation.surface: A list of a builder's tools and materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' sits beside 'mortar' as if it were a tool; it is the verb meaning to defeat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: grout is a thin mortar used to fill the gaps between tiles.

clue.text: Omnipresent upper-class vehicle touring one South American capital

indicators.note: a bus touring a place goes all round it, so its letters surround what follows

parts.note: U = upper-class, as in U and non-U
a bus is a vehicle; it goes around what follows
I = one, the Roman numeral
the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A posh coach seems to be everywhere as it tours a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' reads as a determiner, 'one capital'; it is a letter of its own, the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something ubiquitous is found everywhere at once, which is omnipresent.

clue.text: According to Spooner, Starmer veto for this container

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the starting sounds of words

parts.note: Keir is Starmer's first name; it takes the B sound from the next word
a veto is a ban; it takes the K sound from Keir

explanation.surface: A political note about the Prime Minister blocking something.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Labour leader and Prime Minister, so the surface's politician supplies a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is a metal can that holds beer, one kind of container.

clue.text: Computer programmers drawing in primarily gifted, eccentric oldies

indicators.note: the outer word draws the letter inside it

parts.note: people who write computer code

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter

parts.note: first letter of Gifted

explanation.surface: Talented software developers are recruiting quirky elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' looks like it describes the programmers; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British: codgers are old men, usually thought of as odd or cantankerous, so eccentric oldies.

clue.text: Note on puss that is to get punished

indicators.note: in an across entry, A on B puts A after B

parts.note: puss = cat
a chit is a short note or voucher

explanation.surface: A message pinned to the cat means it is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a musical letter; it is a whole short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: you'll catch it when your mother gets home means you will be scolded or punished.

clue.text: Icy pellet welcomes shade

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet or welcome them
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A frozen pellet gladly receives some shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcomes' looks like a link word; it is a piece of wordplay, and a neat one beside the icy definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a hailstone is a small ball of ice falling as hail.

clue.text: Glum is a queen over Arabic poems of mourning

indicators.note: turned over, the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: glum = sad
taken as written
Q = queen, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A downcast queen weeps over sorrowful Arabic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: An obscure word, so trust the wordplay letter by letter; 'over' looks like 'about' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose definition by use: the qasida is a classical Arabic ode form, often used for elegy and lament.

clue.text: Take in broadcast about barrier

indicators.note: one word goes about, i.e. around, the other

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Listeners absorb a radio programme about a border wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio; it is the old farming sense, scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to swallow food is to take it in, and to swallow a story is to believe it.

clue.text: Donkey consuming just what is needed, a tortilla

indicators.note: the outer word eats, i.e. contains, the inner one

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey
'it' = just the thing, exactly what is needed

explanation.surface: A donkey eats only what it needs, which turns out to be a tortilla.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the answer is Spanish for 'little donkey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a burrito is a flour tortilla rolled around a filling.

clue.text: Speedy warship changes top, becoming an aggressive fighter

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is swapped for another

parts.note: a cruiser is a fast warship; its first letter C is replaced by B

explanation.surface: A fast warship refits and becomes a battler.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter comes in; the definition and crossers show C becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a bruiser is a big, tough man who likes a fight.

clue.text: Valuable fibre unknown in fancy tile

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately worked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: TILE rearranged
x = an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A precious thread is found in a decorative tile.
explanation.walkthrough: An obscure word, so the wordplay must be trusted; the Toughie allows it because every letter is clued.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: ixtle is a strong fibre from Mexican agave plants, valued for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Letter of thanks following article

indicators.note: a thing following another comes after it, so the thanks goes after the article

parts.note: the definite article
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you note written after reading a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter of thanks' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Letter', a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Hesitation admitted by a student, a group of students and an ex-student

indicators.note: the hesitation is let in, i.e. placed inside

parts.note: A as written, then L = learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the sound of hesitating
the National Union of Students, the UK students' union

explanation.surface: A campus scene with a hesitant student, the students' union and a former student.
explanation.walkthrough: Three kinds of student in one clue, but only the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin borrowing: an alumnus is a former pupil or graduate of a school or university.

clue.text: Nick's drama covering end of militant Conservative

indicators.note: the drama covers, i.e. goes around, the letters
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
last letter of militanT
C = Conservative

explanation.surface: A man called Nick has written a play about a hardline Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as a man's name; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nick is a small cut, and so is a notch.

clue.text: Raised money used at first for military group

indicators.note: at first means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of Used

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word makes it read upwards

parts.note: tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds collected were spent first on an army outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised money' reads as fundraising; 'Raised' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a unit is any organised body of troops, such as a company or battalion.

clue.text: Exaggerates merits of measures backing series of balls

indicators.note: the measures back up, i.e. come behind, the series of balls

parts.note: in cricket an over is a series of six balls
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Someone overstates how good certain cricket measures are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts a reversal; here it means supporting from behind, so the measures go second.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: to oversell something is to praise it beyond its real merits.

clue.text: Point of moving north

indicators.note: the letters move into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: The purpose of heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as purpose or a compass point; it is a sharp one.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a thorn is a sharp point on a plant stem.

clue.text: Industrial waste local lasses turned over

indicators.note: a word turned over runs backwards

parts.note: a dialect or informal word for girls

explanation.surface: Local girls sift through factory waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals a regional form of the word for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: slag is the glassy waste left after smelting metal ore.

clue.text: Most dark-hued dilapidated sweatshirt

indicators.note: a dilapidated thing is falling apart, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A very dark, worn-out sweatshirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one faded garment; the first two words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of swarthy, which means dark-complexioned or dark in colour.
